title: THREE KINGDOMS: STRATEGY SIMULATOR
summary: Three Kingdoms Strategy Simulator is an AI-native historical strategy title. Every NPC possesses independent cognition and persistent long-term memory. None of the regional warlords are pre-scripted routines hardcoded into the game engine。
about:
Three Kingdoms Strategy Simulator

An AI-powered historical strategy game where every NPC functions as an independent AI Agent. Powered by large language model computation, each character develops a unique mindset rooted in their historical identity and retains long-term persistent memory. Rival factions may forge alliances with you, only to betray and launch surprise attacks later. Dozens of regional lords scheme against one another, vying for dominion over the Central Plains.

As a time-traveler from the future, you can crush rivals with futuristic technological advantages, or secure victory through political marriages, defection bribery, and any stratagem you can conceive. You may also fill your harem and raise heirs to perpetuate your dynastic rule.

The game features a built-in AI credit system: you can spend in-game model points, or input your own personal API key to connect to local or cloud-hosted large models. You hold full control over which AI model to run—more powerful models deliver smarter NPC behavior, while baseline models support complete stable gameplay.

189 AD. You open your eyes, crowned a regional warlord.

Only yesterday you were scrolling through your phone on your commute; today you stand in a Han dynasty audience hall, facing rows of kneeling civil and military officials. Your granaries hold barely enough grain to sustain your troops, and hostile armies from neighboring principalities loom outside your borders, ready to strike at any moment.

No tutorial will guide your next move. For in this realm, your advisors are living, autonomous minds.

Yet you grasp one harsh truth: if you take no action, the coming century will witness one of the bloodiest upheavals in Chinese history. Corpses will litter the wilderness, and not a single chicken will crow across desolated miles. The national population will plummet from over 50 million to fewer than 10 million.

You are a visitor from two millennia ahead. You have studied this chapter of history, and you know how every tragedy unfolds.

That is precisely why you have been brought here.

We have built an unprecedented experiment: to grant genuine independent cognition to in-game characters.

This is no hollow "favorability +10" status feedback, nor rigid branching storytelling where picking Option A locks in Plot B. Over 1,374 historical figures—Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Zhuge Liang, Lü Bu, Sima Yi, to name a few—are driven by large language models, each endowed with distinct personalities, permanent memory, independent judgment, and dynamic emotion.

Every word you exchange with them will be permanently remembered.

Zhuge Liang, your chief strategist, will not remain unconditionally loyal merely because you are the protagonist. If you dismiss his counsel and suffer a crushing defeat, his tone and attitude will shift drastically in all future consultations. If you break a promise to Zhang Fei, he will never place full trust in you again. If you plot with Zhou Yu to divide Jing Province in secret, your private conversation may leak—and resurface as a fatal bargaining chip at the most critical hour.

Your adversaries scheme behind closed doors as well. Cao Cao and Sun Quan may secretly negotiate to partition Jing Province. Yuan Shao and Gongsun Yuan may fight to the last man on the battlefield. Your spies might intercept a confidential letter: Cao Cao pledges to cede the six Jiangdong commanderies to Sun Quan if he aids in the joint campaign.

Is this letter authentic military intelligence, or a trap deliberately planted to mislead you?

You can never be certain. In the Three Kingdoms era, no one deserves absolute trust.
The Arrogance and Consequences of a Time-Traveler

You come from a modern era. You know Cao Cao’s comeback victory against overwhelming odds at Guandu, you know the fire attack that turned the tide at Chibi, and you know Zhuge Liang’s peerless genius as a military advisor.

Yet your arrival has already fractured the original timeline of history.
